html:
The Abenaki are an Algonquian people of northern New England and southern Quebec, part of the Wabanaki Confederacy, "the people of the dawn land". The Eastern Abenaki lived in Maine; the Western Abenaki in Vermont, New Hampshire and Quebec.

They hunted, fished and farmed maize in the river valleys. Epidemics in the early 1600s hit them hard. Allied with New France and its missionaries, they fought New England in a long series of wars from the 1670s to the 1760s. In 1724 English troops destroyed the mission village of Norridgewock and killed its French priest, Sébastien Rale. Many Abenaki moved north to the mission villages of Odanak and Wôlinak in Quebec, which remain their main communities. Related peoples include the Penobscot and the Androscoggin. See also Abenaki.
